blocks.text: A multiple allelic system occurs when a gene has more than two alternative forms (alleles) in a population. This creates more variation in traits.

An example is the human ABO blood group system. It is controlled by one gene (I gene) with three alleles: Iᴬ, Iᴮ, and i. Each person has only two of these alleles. Different combinations produce four blood groups:

blocks.caption: Phenotypes and genotypes of the ABO blood groups

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: In human ABO blood group system, the alleles Iᴬ and Iᴮ also show co-dominance.
